newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end lower in a nervous market.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end lower in a nervous market.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mostly lower, as stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data kept the forex market nervous, traders and analysts said.
Chicago's June National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) and U.S. May new home sales each rose more than expected and initially helped marks and Swiss francs cut losses.

Chicago's NAPM, a precursor to Tuesday's NAPM, climbed to 61.5, compared with average trade estimates for 57.5 and against May's unrevised 56.8. Home sales rose to an annual rate of 825,000 units, versus estimates of 786,000 units.

The reports indicated that U.S. economic growth remained robust in the last half of the second quarter, contrary to some expectations for a slowdown, and immediately sparked heavy selling in U.S. T-bonds and U.S. stocks.
"There is some speculation that maybe we won't have to wait long until we see higher U.S. rates," Gerry Davies, regional director of forex at Technical Data, said.
Both September marks and September Swiss francs traded at the day's highs of $0.5780, or about 1.7390 spot, and $0.6938, as the selloff of U.S. assets initially unsettled the dollar, Davies said.
Although the dollar sold off, Davies said it was more significant that the currency found a fair amount of bids at 1.7390.
September marks drifted to the lower end of their range, falling through $0.5771 or 1.7425, a dollar/mark resistance level. Traders said funds sold several thousand September mark contracts.
Davies said 1.75 spot will be the next major psychological resistance level for the dollar, as the U.S. currency continues to advance against most of the European units.
"If you look at the EMU, it's hard to be terribly bullish," he said.
Meanwhile, September yen scaled back its gains, falling to $0.008822. Support is seen at $0.008809 to $0.008800.

Sterling and Canadian dollars turned negative, but September sterling ended slightly higher. Both currencies are expected to rise in the near- to intermediate-term, traders said. September Mexican peso futures advanced in the afternoon, pushing to the $0.121900 level. One floor trader believes September may climb through resistance at $0.121920 ahead of Mexico's July 6 mid-term elections.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was off $0.000001 at $0.008826, marks were down $0.0017 at $0.5765, Swiss francs were down $0.0033 at $0.6908, sterling was up $0.0010 at $1.6606, Canadian dollars were off $0.0006 at $0.7276, Aussie dollars were up $0.0081 at $0.7542 and pesos rose $0.000350 at $0.122000. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
